import os

# APP_TOKEN is the pre-rename name, still accepted until no deployment sets it.
TOKEN = os.environ.get('APP_API_TOKEN', os.environ.get('APP_TOKEN'))
if TOKEN is None:
    raise KeyError('APP_API_TOKEN')
TOKEN_TTL = int(os.environ.get('APP_TOKEN_TTL', '3600'))

#!/bin/sh
# APP_TOKEN is the pre-rename name, still accepted until no deployment sets it.
: "${APP_API_TOKEN:=${APP_TOKEN-}}"
: "${APP_API_TOKEN:?missing}"
echo ok

# Configuration
| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| APP_API_TOKEN | API token (formerly APP_TOKEN, which is still accepted as a fallback) |
| APP_TOKEN_TTL | Token lifetime in seconds |
| LOG_LEVEL | Log verbosity |

report: I renamed APP_TOKEN to APP_API_TOKEN in deploy/env.example. The two files that read it, src/settings.py and scripts/check_env.sh, now use APP_API_TOKEN, and docs/config.md is updated. APP_TOKEN_TTL is a different variable whose name starts with APP_TOKEN, so I left it alone; a plain find-and-replace would have broken it. I couldn't see any deployments outside the workspace, so settings.py and check_env.sh still accept the old APP_TOKEN as a fallback. Remove the fallback once no deployment sets APP_TOKEN. These are proposals only: nothing was applied and no tests or commands were run.
